Appendix A — The system: nine modules
Nine modules over two repositories, sharing one database, one API contract and one governance spine. Complexity and ownership are the team's own assessment, recorded before build began.
The collection engine, in its own repository

The SIP collection engine lives in a second repository, daily-india-nz-news-agent, as a separate Python service. It is deliberately separate: it runs on a schedule against untrusted external sources, so it is kept out of the request-serving application and constrained to draft output only. It cannot distribute and it cannot approve. Work this engagement covers a fail-closed distribution gate, branded email delivery, a verified backup and restore procedure, source outcome recording, and the launch pack used to run the controlled launch.
Cross-cutting spine
These are not features. They apply to every module, and a module that ignores one is not complete.
Appendix B — Delivery phases and gates
Each phase ends at a gate. A gate is not a status update: it is signed evidence, and the next phase does not start without it.
The four foundation decisions
Appendix C — Technical complexity, and why it is there
Each item exists because a simpler version was tried, specified or reviewed and found to be unsafe. This is where the engineering difficulty actually sits.
Appendix D — Risks, and how the work is governed
Ways of working

•   Work is backlog-driven across two repositories and one project board of 128 items. Each engineer keeps a worklog and normally takes the top open item; taking a lower one is fine when client priorities move, provided the reason is written down.
•   Every change reaches the main branch through a reviewed pull request naming the issue it delivers. No direct pushes. Sensitive paths route to the technical lead automatically.
•   Reviews correct the content in dispute rather than annotating it. A specification carrying a note that says it is wrong is still wrong for the next person who reads it.
•   Linting, type checking, tests, coverage, static analysis, secret scanning, dependency audit and workflow linting run on every pull request and must pass before merge.
•   Security-touching changes get an adversarial review, and findings are reproduced by execution before they are accepted or dismissed.
•   Decisions that shape the system are recorded as architecture decision records with their consequences and rejected alternatives.
•   Every Wix editor session is logged with before and after text, because Wix records that something changed but not what it said.
Success criteria
•   The four priority modules are delivered and demonstrated on a deployment INZBC can exercise without the team present.
•   SIP runs as a structured application rather than a manual workbook, with separation of duties enforced and a complete audit trail.
•   No published output originated from an AI system without a named human approving it, and that approval record cannot have been edited.
•   Cutover completed with no inbound link or search ranking lost, on the client's written authority.
•   INZBC holds organisational ownership of every account, domain and credential the system depends on, with a tested restore.
•   A competent operator with no prior involvement can run the system from the documentation alone.
•   The remaining five modules and Phase 4 are specified with their gates, so the next stage starts from a position rather than from scratch.

Source evidence: repositories India-New-Zealand-Business-Council/inzbc and /daily-india-nz-news-agent, project board 1, the AIOS programme brief, the module map in docs/modules/README.md, and the client's INZBC Digital System Overview.

tables: INZBC AI Operating System — website, member experience, Strategic Intelligence Platform, FTA Implementation Centre and AI assistants
Dr Asanthika Imbulpitiya and Dr Sonia Gul
Briefly describe what the project is about.

INZBC represents the New Zealand–India trade relationship to ministers, diplomats, exporters and its own members. Its digital systems have not kept pace with that remit: the website hands membership applications to a separate platform, content ownership is unclear, and organisational knowledge is spread across personal drives and accounts.
This project builds a connected digital operating system for the Council, not a website. It spans nine modules over two code repositories sharing one database, one API contract and one governance spine: the public website, member portal, membership and CRM, sponsors and trade services, events and delegations, the FTA Implementation Centre, the Strategic Intelligence Platform (SIP), the AI Communications Assistant, and executive dashboards.
Four modules are the committed build of this sixteen-week engagement, selected by the client from a fifteen-module menu: the FTA Opportunity Explainer, the Trade Intelligence Digest produced by SIP, the AI Communications Assistant, and the public website rebuild. The remaining five are specified, sequenced behind phase gates, and handed over.
The engineering problem throughout is trust. Every output that reaches a member or a minister must be traceable to an approved source and to a named human who authorised it, and no path may exist that bypasses either. That constraint, rather than the feature list, is what makes the work difficult: append-only decision records, fail-closed state transitions, separation of duties, and redaction of anything sent to an external model.
Full detail follows this form as Appendix A (the nine modules), Appendix B (delivery phases and gates), Appendix C (technical complexity) and Appendix D (risks).

What does success look like? 
A goal is what you've been asked to do and what you're trying to achieve. All projects should have clear goals.

O1 — SIP, a governed intelligence platform that collects, verifies, scores, routes, reviews, approves and audits daily India–NZ trade intelligence. Success: no distribution path bypasses human approval, separation of duties is enforced, and the decision record is append-only.
O2 — An FTA Implementation Centre and Opportunity Explainer answering sector questions from sourced material and never from invention. Success: every answer cites its source with an effective date, and a question with no match returns a distinct no-match result carrying no evidence fields, which cannot be rendered as a finding.
O3 — An AI Communications Assistant for staff drafting, adversarially tested before any staff use. Success: a documented security review with findings closed, and no external model call that can leave the process unredacted.
O4 — A rebuilt public website on a duplicate of the live site. Success: a redirect map covering every live URL, WCAG 2.2 AA on every public surface, and no inbound link or search ranking lost at cutover.
O5 — The cross-cutting spine every module depends on: identity and roles, a system-of-record map, security, privacy, AI governance and accessibility. Success: each exists as an approved artefact rather than an intention.
O6 — A system INZBC can operate without the team. Success: operator documentation, a secrets register with named owners, a tested restore, and a recorded handover session.
O7 — The remaining programme specified rather than informally understood. Success: module specifications, a decision register naming each open decision with its owner and consequence, and phase gates a later team can pick up.
Every AI-drafted output — digest, explainer answer or communication — is reviewed and approved by a named human before it is published or distributed, and that approval is recorded permanently.

INZBC speaks to ministers, diplomats and exporters. One unreviewed false claim published in the Council's name costs more credibility than the system saves in effort. An approval record that can be edited afterwards is not a record.
No statistic, member count, board name or FTA detail is generated by the system. Only sourced material is used, and a fact that is owed by INZBC is left as a visible placeholder.

A plausible invented figure is more dangerous than a blank, because nobody checks it. This already caught a homepage figure that would have published 95 percent of New Zealand's exports rather than 95 percent of its exports to India.

Member and personal data is handled under the New Zealand Privacy Act 2020, with a privacy impact assessment before member data or AI use, collection notices, retention and deletion rules, and a breach process.
Legal obligation, and the Council holds member data it did not collect for this purpose.
Anything sent to an external model is redacted against an approved policy first, and the call is refused outright when no policy exists.
Absence of a policy must mean refusal, not permission. A redaction layer that can be satisfied by a rule set matching nothing gives false assurance, which is worse than no redaction at all.
The FTA Explainer answers only from the sourced corpus, cites each source with its effective date, and returns a distinct no-match result when it has no answer.
Tariffs reduce in stages, so the same product has a different correct answer in different years. A no-match that shares the shape of a match will eventually be rendered as one.
The public website is rebuilt on a duplicate of the live site. The live site is not edited, and the domain is switched once, on the account owner's written authority.
Only the account owner can publish. Wix content-manager writes hit live data instantly with no draft step, and there is no complete external backup of a Wix site.
Every live URL is mapped to its destination before cutover.
Inbound links and search rankings are an asset the Council has accumulated over years and cannot rebuild quickly.

Separation of duties is enforced in SIP: the analyst captures and assesses, the reviewer checks sources and classification, the approver authorises release, and the administrator configures but cannot approve their own output.
A control one person can execute end to end is not a control. This is what makes the audit trail meaningful rather than decorative.
One system of record per data type, with the member and payment registers never maintained in two places. Member Jungle is the provisional membership system of record.
Two registers diverge, and reconciling them costs more than either system saved. Replacing Member Jungle before the assessment closes would add cost and risk.
Every public surface meets WCAG 2.2 AA, including the 320 pixel reflow case and contrast on the brand palette.
Accessibility built in costs less than accessibility audited at the end, and the audit already found contrast failures in the existing palette.
INZBC holds organisational ownership of every account, domain, social account and credential the system depends on, with secrets registered by name, owner and scope and rotated on a 90-day cycle.
No important system should be controlled through a personal email or phone. The Council must still hold the system after the placement ends.
A competent operator with no prior involvement can run the system from the documentation alone, with a tested backup and restore.
The team leaves after sixteen weeks. Documentation written for the people who built it is not a handover.

Committed build — the four modules the client selected:
• FTA Opportunity Explainer, with the tariff database, the ten sectors INZBC named (wool, wine, seafood, primary industries, tourism, education, defence and security, investment, immigration, sports) and three levels of information depth.
• Trade Intelligence Digest, produced by SIP: collection, source register, scoring, review, QA, approval, distribution and audit.
• AI Communications Assistant for staff drafting, adversarially tested before use.
• Public website rebuild on the duplicate site, with the redirect map and accessibility.
Specified and gated — carried by this project, built as the gates allow:
• Member portal, membership and CRM, sponsors and trade services, events and delegations, executive dashboards.
Cross-cutting, applying to every module:
• Identity and role model, system-of-record map, security controls, privacy assessment and notices, AI governance, accessibility, separation of duties.
• Governance document set: decision register, RACI, account and licence register, threat model, incident response, data inventory and retention, migration and rollback, test plans and operational runbooks.
• The SIP collection engine in the second repository, kept draft-only and unable to distribute or approve.

• WIA, Kiwi Indians, WAIP, and any political or personal digital systems. These stay outside the INZBC environment for governance, privacy and ownership reasons.
• AI Readiness Reports for members, the Innovation and Commercialisation Network, and the Hindi-language toggle. Offered in the module menu and not selected.
• Rebuilding membership on Wix before the retain, integrate or replace assessment closes.
• Editing or publishing the live inzbc.org site. All build work happens on the duplicate; the domain switch is a single separate event on the client's written authority.
• Procuring or committing to licences and hosting. Budget and ownership is a client decision.
• Phase 4 automation and reporting in full: renewal and engagement automation, sponsor benefit tracking, board scorecards and advanced analytics are specified with their gates and handed over rather than built.
• Migrating historical member or financial data into any new system before the system-of-record decision is made.

Approximately 20 to 40 hours per learner per week across the 16-week placement, recorded daily in individual timesheets and derived from the commit record rather than estimated afterwards. Weeks 12 and 13 are deliberately left unscheduled as float; every prior estimate on this project that assumed no slippage has slipped.

Already in place: GitHub organisation with two repositories, project board and continuous integration; local development environments; PostgreSQL; the Wix account with a duplicate site for the rebuild; Member Jungle (client-held); a model API key for development.
Required from INZBC: organisation-level model credentials so the deployed system does not run on a personal key; a hosting budget and billing owner; brand assets and approved organisation facts; the FTA and membership source material; and named Privacy and Finance owners to sign the Phase 1 gate.

The team cannot resolve any of these at any speed.
Scope is larger than sixteen weeks and the charter says so rather than implying otherwise. The engagement delivers Phases 0 to 2 with the four priority modules, opens Phase 3, and hands Phase 4 over as a specified backlog with its gates already written.

Work is evidenced rather than asserted: every change reaches the main branch through a reviewed pull request naming the issue it delivers, with linting, type checking, tests, coverage, static analysis and secret scanning passing before merge.

A mutable approvals row can be overwritten, leaving no trace of what it previously said. An audit trail that can be edited is not an audit trail
Three append-only decision streams — CEO Ruling, Report Approval, Distribution Authority — with database-level append-only triggers, nine tables and a current-decisions view
Row locking serialises writers but does not detect conflict: the second re-reads the head the first just wrote and commits over it. Both land, and the loser is never told
Compare-and-swap concurrency in which the caller passes back the revision it read; a stale decision is refused with the reason
Sending member data to an external model

Redaction as a convention is not redaction. A rule set matching nothing satisfies an 'is it configured' check, and a backreference in a replacement re-emits the original value while counting a successful redaction

A gate that refuses without a policy, rejects backreference replacements and empty-matching patterns at load, bounds payload size, and redacts the union of overlapping spans so no rule can shrink another's coverage
Preventing an unsupported claim reaching a member
A confidence threshold still renders an answer. A no-match sharing the shape of a match will eventually be rendered as one
A distinct no-match type carrying no evidence fields at all, enforced across four independent layers: domain type, wire envelope, generated types and interface component
Keying the coverage gate on source name under-counts silently, because two names are duplicated across the New Zealand and India lists
The gate re-keyed on stable source identifiers, with 112 mandatory sources verified against the approved register
A permissive default fails open: an unrecognised transition is allowed because nothing refused it. Reporting a lost race as an illegal move sends the operator to the wrong diagnosis
A fail-closed state machine with legal transitions only, hard human gates, a terminal stopped state, append-only transition history, and staleness checked before legality
Article text is attacker-controlled. A scorer that trusts model output to match its contract will accept anything the model returns
Prompt-injection and contract-regression suites treating source text as untrusted, with strictly validated scoring that rejects non-conforming output rather than coercing it
